instructions: Cut the potatoes in half, or into quarters if they're bigger than a walnut. Transfer them to a medium pot, cover with about 1 inch of cold water and stir in the 1 tbsp salt.
Set the pot over medium-high heat. When the water boils, turn the heat down to medium and simmer for about 15 minutes, until a knife slides into a potato with no resistance.
Meanwhile, put the eggs in a small saucepan and cover them with about 1 inch of cold water. Set it over high heat and bring to a rapid boil.
Boil the eggs for 1 minute, then take the pan off the heat, cover it and leave it for 10 minutes.

While the potatoes and eggs cook, make the vinaigrette. In a small bowl, whisk 1 tbsp Dijon mustard with 1 tbsp red wine vinegar and a pinch of salt. Whisk in the olive oil a little at a time until it looks creamy.
Wash and dry the lettuce and tear it into large pieces. Cut the ham into wide strips, cut the Comte into 1/2-inch cubes and slice the mushrooms thinly.
Chop 8 cornichons and mince the chives.
Drain the potatoes and rinse them under cold water until they're cool. Cool the eggs under cold running water, peel them and cut each one into quarters.
Divide the lettuce among 4 plates. Top each with ham, Comte, mushrooms, cornichons, potatoes and the 4 egg quarters from one egg.
Whisk the vinaigrette again and spoon it over the plates. Scatter the chives over, add a few turns of black pepper and serve right away.
method_notes: Pardon Your French (the lead) and The French Cooking Academy agree on the base: crisp lettuce, thick ham, a hard mountain cheese and hard-boiled eggs in a Dijon vinaigrette, dressed at the last minute. They differ on potatoes: the lead has boiled new potatoes plus mushrooms and cornichons, the Academy leaves them out, so the potato-and-Comté version here follows the lead. The lead says French vinaigrette without an amount, so the dressing ratio is the standard 1 mustard, 1 vinegar, 3 oil. For lunch boxes, pack the dressing separately; once dressed the salad is best within 2 to 3 hours. Neither source has 20 ratings (the lead has 2) and RecipeTin Eats has no version, so this is flagged as a fallback.
